sentences.text: Yongjinglong was an extinct genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur.
This genus contains only one species, Yongjinglong datangi, and represents a medium-sized sauropod.
The animal possessed long, spoon-shaped premaxillary teeth.
Its neck and front back vertebrae featured large, deep air-filled depressions covering the entire sides of the bones.
Ridges on the middle back vertebrae created a unique pattern resembling the letters "XI" with the cross in front.
The shoulder blade was extremely long with exceptionally straight front and rear edges when viewed from the side.
The holotype was discovered in 2008 by Li Daqing and You Hailu beside the G75 Highway.
This specimen, catalogued as GSGM ZH(08)-04, consists of a partial postcranial skeleton and three teeth representing a subadult individual.
Li-Guo Li, Da-Qing Li, Hai-Lu You, and Peter Dodson formally named the genus in 2014 after the historical Yongjing County and the Chinese word for "dragon".
In 2014, researchers placed Yongjinglong within the group Titanosauria.

A 2019 revision of Chinese titanosaurs later resolved the species as deeply nested within Euhelopodidae, as a sister taxon to Huanghetitan and Ruyangosaurus, or within a clade including Euhelopus, Erketu, and Gobititan.
Yongjinglong lived during the Early Cretaceous in the Lanzhou-Minhe Basin of Gansu Province, China.
Its existence spanned between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago, covering the Barremian to the Aptian stages.
There is a debate regarding Yongjinglong's classification, with a 2019 study suggesting it belongs to Euhelopodidae rather than Titanosauria.
